text:
jun: Quick flag  canary reranker v5-int8 on clinical-holdout shows NDCG ~flat (+0.2%) but MRR -3.2%. Drop concentrated in queries <=5 tokens and title-like candidates. Anyone free to eyeball?

kai: Can you paste the slice table or a tiny csv?

jun: Uploaded summary and a small disagreements dump: s3://bench/rerank/3141592653/summary.csv and s3://bench/rerank/3141592653/disagree_20.jsonl

```
model,cohort,ndcg,mrr,top1
float32,clinical-holdout,0.648,0.521,0.57
int8,clinical-holdout,0.649,0.504,0.50
float32,web-holdout,0.615,0.507,0.52
int8,web-holdout,0.614,0.505,0.51
```

anya: Short-queries and title-like candidates rings tokenizer or short-seq KV cache boundary issues. Did the canary use the exact same tokenizer and harness config?

jun: Harness config diff shows one flag changed: "token_norm_maps" had an extra mapping for zero-width joiner in the int8 branch. Also a scaling tweak in the int8 scorer (logit_scale=0.995 vs 1.0).

ioscar: Two cheap ablations: (1) int8 with float tokenizer (force parity), (2) int8 with float final linear (mixed-last-layer). Which do you want first?

jun: Kicking both on a 12k sample. Jobs: 3141592666 (A), 3141592677 (B). CI: https://ci.redwood.prod/jobs/3141592666

ci-bot: Job 3141592666 queued. Job 3141592677 queued.

kai: Also add a micro-slice to dashboards for query_len<=5 and title-like heuristics (capitalization + colon + short). We miss these in rollouts.

ci-bot: Job 3141592666 completed. Logs: https://ci.redwood.prod/jobs/3141592666/logs

jun: Early peek: A (int8 + float-tokenizer) recovers ~1.9% MRR on the short-query slice. B (mixed-last-layer) recovers ~0.8%. Looks like tokenizer mapping was primary, scorer scaling adds residual jitter.

anya: Action items: 1) revert token_norm_map difference in quant branch, 2) add tokenization-parity CI check to canary harness, 3) add query_len<=5 micro-slice to canary dashboard, 4) keep mixed-last-layer as fallback mitigation.

ioscar: I'll file the small GT ticket and add the checklist items. Also propose a pre-token canonicalizer for clinical cohort to normalize invisible unicode.

jun: Thanks 44d will re-run full canary after the revert and post final numbers here.
